stories.title: Worth & Associates Acquires 108K-SF San Antonio Office Campus
stories.excerpt: Worth & Associates acquired The Commons at Concord Park, a four-building, 108,116 square-foot office campus located at 300 E. Sonterra Blvd in San Antonio’s Stone Oak submarket. It brings the company’s total owned portfolio to 3 million square feet. The Commons at Concord Park currently features 17,131 square feet of available space for lease, with suites ranging from 1,254 to 9,790 square feet. The campus is 85% occupied and includes a mix of single-story and two-story office buildings designed to accommodate a variety of professional office users. The property’s diverse tenant mix includes businesses spanning construction, logistics, medical research, healthcare and physical therapy services, reflecting the campus’s flexibility and broad market appeal. Worth & Associates immediately assumed leasing and management following the acquisition. The firm plans to make several capital improvements throughout the property. Shawn Gulley represented Worth & Associates, and Todd Mills at Cushman & Wakefield represented The Commons at Concord Park in the transaction. Brookwood is listed as a former owner. Connect Texas Multifamily in Dallas on August 13 brings together the owners, developers, brokers, investors, and lenders shaping the future of Texas multifamily for a day of market intelligence, networking, and actionable insights. Join 300+ decision-makers and be part of the conversations driving the Texas multifamily market. Register today: www.ConnectTXMF2026.com. bullets: Worth & Associates acquired 108K-SF office campus in San Antonio Stone Oak.
Property 85% occupied; 17K SF available; diverse tenant mix (construction, logistics, healthcare).
Minimal relevance to multifamily development; office-focused transaction.
stories.summary: Worth & Associates acquired The Commons at Concord Park, a four-building, 108,116-square-foot office campus at 300 E. Sonterra Blvd in San Antonio's Stone Oak submarket. The property is 85% occupied with 17,131 SF of available space and a diverse tenant mix spanning construction, logistics, medical research, healthcare, and physical therapy. Worth plans capital improvements and assumed leasing and management immediately post-acquisition.
stories.impact: Minimal impact on multifamily development. This is an office transaction in a submarked with no noted demand pressure or supply constraints that would signal timing for residential development.

stories.title: CBRE Reports Strong Q2 Earnings Amid Data Center Revenues, Office Leasing Gains
stories.excerpt: Surging data center services revenue and a rebound in U.S. office leasing stood out in CBRE’s strong second-quarter results for 2026. During a Wednesday morning earnings call, the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm reported $11.2 billion in second-quarter revenue, roughly in line with analysts’ estimates. Revenue grew annually by 15.5 percent, and increased over its first-quarter results by roughly 6.6 percent. CBRE’s earnings beat analysts’ expectations, with core earnings per share of $1.56. Adjusted profit rose to $459 million from $361 million a year earlier, stripping out one-off line items like fire-safety repairs on U.K. buildings. The firm’s second-quarter report included more than $700 million in revenue from data center services. U.S. office leasing notched a second-quarter record, too, in a welcome signal of continued commercial recovery. CBRE’s more volatile segments, like property sales, mortgage origination and leasing, saw revenue growth of 19 percent year-over-year. U.S. leasing revenues spiked by 24 percent, led by office and industrial activity. Most notably, U.S. office leasing generated its highest-ever second-quarter revenue, according to Emma Giamartino, CBRE’s chief financial officer. The strength was driven by gateway markets, as well as space upgrades from financial and legal tenants. CBRE’s global property sales saw increased revenues of 20 percent, with the U.S. tracking a 24 percent increase across most property types. Despite the strong performance, there’s still room for recovery. “On the leasing side, we’re still not back to 2019 levels,” Giamartino said. “We see there’s more room to go this year, and that will extend into next year. And on the sales side, we’re still pretty early. bullets: CBRE Q2 2026 revenue $11.2B, +15.5% YoY; data center services exceeded $700M.
U.S. office leasing hit second-quarter record; leasing revenue +24% YoY.
Strong capital markets activity and transaction pipeline indicate improving fundamentals across sectors.
stories.summary: CBRE reported $11.2 billion in Q2 2026 revenue, up 15.5% year-over-year, with core EPS of $1.56 beating analyst expectations. Data center services exceeded $700 million in revenue, and U.S. office leasing hit a second-quarter record, with leasing revenues spiking 24% YoY. The firm's volatile segments (property sales, mortgage origination, leasing) saw 19% revenue growth YoY.
stories.impact: Rising capital markets activity and strong leasing velocity signal improving financing availability and transaction confidence across CRE, likely supportive for multifamily acquisitions and refinancings. However, the surge in data center services reflects capital flow away from traditional office/residential; multifamily developers should monitor whether office-to-residential conversion opportunities will emerge in secondary markets where office demand remains soft.

stories.title: BXP Secures $1.2B Construction Loan for 343 Madison Avenue Office Tower
stories.excerpt: BXP, the largest Class A office owner in the country, has landed a $1.2 billion construction loan to build its 930,000-square-foot office tower development at 343 Madison Avenue in Midtown, the real estate investment trust (REIT) announced Wednesday morning during its second-quarter earnings call. The financing for BXP’s 46-story development came from Wells Fargo, Bank of America Securities, Bank of New York Mellon and J.P. Morgan Chase. The loan has a four-year initial term, plus a one-year extension option, according to BXP. Once construction is completed — a finish date is set for 2029 — the $2 billion project at 343 Madison Avenue will feature offices, dining spaces, terraces and plenty of amenities. The anticipated tower just west of Grand Central Terminal is also already 50 percent pre-leased, after insurance and investment giant C.V. Starr signed a 275,000-square-foot deal in October to anchor the property, and law firm McDermott Will & Schulte took roughly 150,000 square feet there in April. Starr later expanded its initial lease by another two full floors. BXP executives said during Wednesday’s earnings call that the firm is in negotiations with two more prospective tenants, which would bring the building to nearly 70 percent pre-leased. CEO Owen Thomas said the REIT will lease the rest of the floors closer to delivery to secure “market-leading rents.” “The pricing power in Manhattan remains quite favorable to landlords, and it is expanding geographically,” Hilary Spann, executive vice president of BXP’s New York region, said during the call. “We are getting inbound interest at our highest-quality buildings and at 343 Madison at rents that are consistently 10 to 15 percent above where they were last year. … And, in the lower stack of our buildings where rents are slightly more affordable, we’re still seeing 20 percent increases year-over-year, and that is fundamentally because there’s a lack of available space in the market. stories.summary: BXP, the largest Class A office REIT, secured a $1.2 billion construction loan from Wells Fargo, Bank of America Securities, BNY Mellon, and JPMorgan Chase for its 930,000-square-foot, 46-story office tower at 343 Madison Avenue in Midtown Manhattan. The $2 billion project, set to complete in 2029, is already 50% pre-leased after C.V. Starr committed to 275,000 SF and McDermott Will & Schulte took 150,000 SF. stories.impact: BXP's ability to secure $1.2B in construction financing at scale signals strong lender appetite for trophy Manhattan assets, but the focus on office (even Class A in prime Midtown) reflects residual capital concentration in office. Limited direct multifamily impact, though sustained office construction in Manhattan may compete for labor and materials in the region.

stories.title: Newmark Tops Earnings Forecasts Aided by 16% Capital Markets Boost
stories.excerpt: Newmark continued its 2026 momentum as a leading global real estate advisory firm this year by topping earnings forecasts for a second straight quarter thanks largely to a boost in its capital markets investment business. The company reported adjusted earnings per share of 39 cents for the second quarter to beat out Wall Street forecasts of 38 cents. Revenue also soared 17 percent from a year ago to $884 million, a second-quarter record for Newmark and higher than analysts’ estimates of $852.28 million. “Given Newmark’s strong results and healthy transaction pipeline, we continue to expect double-digit top- and bottom-line growth for the third consecutive year in 2026,” Newmark CEO Barry Gosin said during a second-quarter earnings call Wednesday morning. “We also anticipate that our investments in recurring revenue businesses, ongoing international expansion, improving industry fundamentals, and talented professionals will together drive Newmark’s long-term growth and market-share gains.” Capital markets revenues rose 16 percent, which Newmark attributed to a large increase in multifamily investment sales activity, particularly for senior housing and affordable housing assets. Gosin noted that Newmark is the No. 1 investment sales platform in affordable housing with a large percentage of that portfolio composed of properties backed by Section 8 and Low-Income Housing Tax Credits. He said there are strong tailwinds for affordable housing given the bipartisan political support in Washington, D.C., to confront the affordability issue. “It seems to be a popular word these days, and there is no disagreement between the Democrats and the Republicans with respect to the importance of building affordable housing,” Gosin said. “We managed to pick that just as we got into data centers two, three years ago ahead of the curve, which has given us some momentum in terms of multifamily.” The gains to Newmark’s capital markets business from investment sales
bullets: Newmark Q2 2026: revenue $884M (+17% YoY), adjusted EPS 39¢, beat forecasts.
Capital markets revenue +16%; company expects double-digit growth third consecutive year.
Strong transaction pipeline and capital markets momentum support active acquisition/disposition market.
stories.summary: Newmark reported Q2 2026 revenue of $884 million, up 17% year-over-year and a second-quarter record, beating analyst estimates of $852.28 million. Adjusted earnings per share came in at 39 cents, beating Wall Street forecasts of 38 cents. CEO Barry Gosin attributed growth to a 16% boost in capital markets investment business and expects double-digit top- and bottom-line growth for the third consecutive year in 2026.
stories.impact: Robust transaction advisory and capital markets activity signals strong deal flow velocity and lender confidence, creating favorable conditions for multifamily acquisitions, dispositions, and refinancings across major markets. The firm's international expansion and recurring revenue growth suggest capital availability for development and value-add plays.

stories.title: Wolverine Mixed-Use Project Advancing in Arlington
stories.excerpt: A new four-story, mixed-use development featuring apartments and a variety of shops, offices and restaurant space is planned for Downtown Arlington.  Under the agreement between the city of Arlington and Wolverine Interests, Wolverine would invest at least $60 million by 2029 to redevelop the 500 and 600 blocks of West Abram Street and the 400 and 500 blocks of West Main Street for the mixed-use project. The future development is required to include: a minimum of 248 multifamily units a minimum of 15,000 square feet of commercial space, including office, retail, food and beverage and/or personal services a multi-level parking garage with at least 300 parking spaces In return for meeting performance requirements, the City would reimburse the developer up to $2,550,000 for eligible costs. The first item involves completing demolition of all existing structures and site remediation by Dec.15, 2026. The post Wolverine Mixed-Use Project Advancing in Arlington appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Wolverine Interests planning $60M mixed-use (apartments + retail/office) in Downtown Arlington by 2029.
City of Arlington offering up to $2.55M reimbursement for eligible costs under redevelopment agreement.
Project targets 500/600 blocks West Abram, 400/500 blocks West Main; demolition due Dec. 15, 2026.
stories.summary: Wolverine Interests and the City of Arlington entered an agreement for Wolverine to invest at least $60 million by 2029 to redevelop four downtown blocks (500 and 600 blocks of West Abram Street and 400 and 500 blocks of West Main Street) as a four-story mixed-use development featuring apartments, retail, offices, and restaurants. The city will reimburse the developer up to $2.55 million for eligible costs upon meeting performance requirements. Demolition of all existing structures and site remediation is due by December 15, 2026.
stories.impact: Tax increment financing (TIF) or cost-reimbursement incentives in Arlington downtown signal municipal appetite for residential-led mixed-use infill, likely driven by demand for walkable urban housing in a fast-growing DFW submarket. Public investment via incentives reduces developer risk and accelerates entitlements, making downtown Arlington a target submarket for mid-rise multifamily development over the next 2–3 years as supply lags demand in the region.

stories.title: Bill Ackman’s Foundation Acquiring Two Upper West Side Buildings to House Brain Research Center
stories.excerpt: Bill Ackman’s Pershing Square Foundation will pay $260 million to acquire two Upper West Side buildings that will house a brain research facility, according to published reports. The foundation acquired 125 West End Ave., which currently houses a 400,000-square-foot life sciences and research campus known as West End Labs, for $190 million, and has signed a $70-million contract for the neighboring 320 W. 66th St., along with additional development rights. If Ackman exercises the development rights, the brain research facility could span 700,000 square feet at full buildout, Fortune magazine reported. To be known as the Ackman Oxman Institute, the complex could eclipse the Rockefeller Institute for Medical Research and other significant health research facilities in New York City. The timeline for the research center’s opening is not known. However, it will be developed in partnership with Mount Sinai Hospital System. The Ackman Oxman Institute’s board is working on hiring its first CEO, Ackman told Fortune. Pictured: West End Labs. Photo courtesy of Taconic Investment Partners. The post Bill Ackman’s Foundation Acquiring Two Upper West Side Buildings to House Brain Research Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Foundation acquiring two Upper West Side NYC buildings for $260M.

stories.summary: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Foundation is acquiring two Upper West Side buildings for $260 million to establish the Ackman Oxman Institute, a brain research facility. The foundation paid $190 million for 125 West End Avenue (currently West End Labs, a 400,000-SF life sciences campus) and signed a $70 million contract for 320 W. 66th Street with additional development rights. At full buildout, the institute could span 700,000 square feet and will be developed in partnership with Mount Sinai Hospital System.
stories.impact: High-net-worth anchor tenancy and institutional capital concentration in Upper West Side life sciences/research real estate signals sustained demand for knowledge-worker housing proximate to major medical institutions in Manhattan. The multi-hundred-million-dollar institutional commitment to build out a major research hub in the Upper West Side should drive rental demand for upscale apartments targeting doctors, researchers, and professionals; multifamily developers should prioritize UWS submarkets and proximity to Mount Sinai for institutional multifamily products.

stories.title: Flexential Secures Land Outside Dallas for 375K-SF Data Center
stories.excerpt: Flexential purchased 110 acres in Kaufman County, Texas, to build its fourth and largest facility in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex. The planned 375,000-square-foot Phase 1 development, southeast of the DFW metro in Talty, has secured power to support 36 MW of capacity for wholesale and multi-tenant colocation workloads, including enterprise and high-density deployments. Site work is expected to begin in early 2027, with first customer availability in late 2028. The 110-acre campus has the potential to support three 36 MW data center buildings, for a total footprint of 108 MW, as additional phases are developed. The acquisition comes after Cushman & Wakefield ranked Dallas the world’s top data center market for development and investment conditions based on more than 20 factors, including power and land availability and construction activity.  The Talty facility will incorporate environmentally responsible, high-efficiency power systems and closed-loop cooling architecture to reduce energy consumption per megawatt of IT load. Talty is about 20 minutes east of Dallas. The post Flexential Secures Land Outside Dallas for 375K-SF Data Center appeared first on Connect CRE.

Multifamily developers should monitor Talty and surrounding Kaufman County submarkets for emerging demand from data center workers and supply-chain proximity; land costs and entitlements in exurban locations will remain attractive relative to prime DFW submarkets.

stories.title: Arrow Arranges $85M Construction Loan for Miami Condo Project
stories.excerpt: Arrow Real Estate Advisors arranged an $85 million construction loan on behalf of Northlink Capital for the development of 7200 Collins Avenue, a 222-unit luxury condominium project in Miami Beach, Florida. The financing, provided by Deutsche Bank, refinances existing debt and will fund the ground-up construction of the 12-story, 274,150-square-foot residential tower through completion. Located at the intersection of Collins Avenue and 72nd Street in Miami Beach’s North Beach neighborhood, the project will offer a collection of studio-, one-, and two-bedroom residences with an average unit size of approximately 489 square feet. Approximately 81% of the residences are priced below $1 million. Amenities will span three levels and include the exclusive 7200 Collins Beach Club, a swimming pool, fitness center, ground-floor retail and food and beverage offerings, and landscaped rooftop sundecks. Arrow Real Estate Advisors’ Morris Betesh, Alex Bailkin, and Matt O’Hanlon arranged the financing. stories.summary: Arrow Real Estate Advisors arranged an $85 million construction loan from Deutsche Bank on behalf of Northlink Capital for 7200 Collins Avenue, a 222-unit luxury condominium project in Miami Beach's North Beach neighborhood. The 12-story, 274,150-square-foot residential tower will feature studios, one-, and two-bedroom units (avg. 489 SF); approximately 81% are priced below $1 million. Amenities include a beach club, pool, fitness center, ground-floor retail, and rooftop sundeck.
stories.impact: Strong construction financing for luxury condo product in Miami Beach signals lender appetite for deed-restricted residential real estate, but condo ownership does not compete directly with rental multifamily. However, $85M financing on a 222-unit project (~$383K per unit) reflects Miami Beach's continued appeal to institutional capital; rental multifamily developers should note that capital is flowing into both rental and for-sale product, suggesting near-term supply constraints in Miami rental stock and potential upside for Class A multifamily development in North Beach and adjacent submarkets.

stories.title: Richman Group, Monadnock Plan to Build 420 Units in East Harlem
stories.excerpt: Get a little place in Harlem and you’ll figure it out. Developers Richman Group and Monadnock Development — in a joint venture — have filed plans with the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB) to construct a 420-unit residential building at 243 East 125th Street in Manhattan’s East Harlem neighborhood. The plan, which was filed July 26 by Richman Group President Kristin Miller, calls for the construction of a 14-story mixed-use building with 648,000 square feet of residential space, 82,000 square feet of commercial space and a 10,700-square-foot community facility. Construction is scheduled to begin by early 2027. Paul Carr of S9 Architecture is the registered architect on the project. Spokespeople for S9 Architecture, Richman Group and Monadnock Development did not immediately respond to requests for comment. If approved, the building’s second through 14th floors would each include between 28 and 38 apartments, according to the DOB plans. The plans also note there will be 65 parking spaces, plus a lot attendant on staff, and bicycle storage for 218 bikes. In addition, the developers are planning for two retail spaces, a social services office, and amenities including a lounge, a gym, a kids playroom and a multipurpose room. The building, on the corner of 125th Street and Second Avenue, would be part of the New York City Economic Development Corporation’s B-East (East 125th Street Development project), a 17,337-square-foot, city-owned property where the city aims to add more mixed-income housing. B-East is part of the broader East 125th Street Development project first approved in 2008, which will ultimately build housing on three land parcels and include about 1.7 million square feet of residential, retail and commercial development. Since the project launched, it has already delivered 451 housing units — including 344 affordable units — and 65,000 square feet of retail space. stories.impact: A 420-unit new-construction rental project in East Harlem signals sustained developer confidence in Manhattan outer-borough rental demand, likely driven by affordability-seeking relocations from Midtown and Upper West Side as those submarkets see institutional/corporate consolidation (e.g., life sciences hubs, trophy office). The project's scale and mixed-use profile (community facility, retail, parking) indicate strong neighborhood absorption fundamentals; multifamily developers should monitor East Harlem and upper Manhattan neighborhoods for similar demand signals and zoning-friendly environments for 14+ story multifamily projects.

stories.title: Vital Infrastructure REIT Buys East New York Outpatient Facility for $90M
stories.excerpt: A Toronto-based real estate investment trust (REIT) has purchased an East New York, Brooklyn, medical facility for $89.9 million. Health care infrastructure REIT Vital Infrastructure Property Trust announced last week that it acquired the 142,249-square-foot East New York Health Hub at 101 Pennsylvania Avenue, which is leased as an outpatient care facility to AdvantageCare Physicians New York. Newmark’s Ben Appel, Adam Spies, Jay Miele, Justin Shepherd, John Nero, Adam Doneger, Matt Berres, Michael Greeley, Ron Ott, Conor Hilton and Drew Martin negotiated on behalf of the buyer and the seller, according to Crain’s New York Business. The seller is Squarefeet.com owner Jonas Rudofsky, a former Newmark director, who has owned the property since 2019, when it was first developed, according to property records. “This acquisition represents another important step in the execution of Vital Infrastructure’s growth strategy,” Zach Vaughan, CEO of Vital Infrastructure, said in a statement. “East New York Health Hub is a modern, institutional-quality, multi-disciplinary health care facility located in a high-barrier market and leased to one of New York’s largest health care networks. The acquisition further strengthens the resilience and quality of our portfolio while expanding our presence in a key U.S. market.” The Newmark team declined to comment. Newmark, however, identified the tenant as nonprofit insurance company EmblemHealth, while Vital said that AdvantageCare still has 11 years remaining on its lease. The building is also leased to New York Cancer & Blood Specialists, Lenox Hill Radiology, New York Health, Advanced Dermatology and Quest Diagnostics, according to the buyer. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Vital Infrastructure Property Trust acquired East New York Health Hub (101 Pennsylvania Ave, Brooklyn) for $89.9M.
142K-SF outpatient facility leased to AdvantageCare Physicians New York; seller Jonas Rudofsky held since 2019.
Healthcare REIT acquisition; no direct multifamily impact.
stories.summary: Toronto-based Vital Infrastructure Property Trust acquired the East New York Health Hub at 101 Pennsylvania Avenue in Brooklyn for $89.9 million. The 142,249-square-foot medical facility is leased to AdvantageCare Physicians New York as an outpatient care center. The property was developed in 2019 and previously held by Jonas Rudofsky (Squarefeet.com owner and former Newmark director). Newmark represented both buyer and seller in the transaction.
stories.impact: Healthcare REIT capital acquisition of neighborhood medical infrastructure in East New York signals institutional appetite for essential-service real estate in outer-borough Brooklyn, but the transaction does not directly affect rental multifamily development. However, healthcare facility anchors in residential neighborhoods drive stable, local-serving job creation and foot traffic; multifamily developers entering East New York should note that institutional medical tenancy strengthens rental demand fundamentals by anchoring neighborhood economic activity.
